At a called meeting of the Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley, Harris County, Georgia, held on the 23rd day of October, 1919, there were present at said meeting S A Goodman, Mayor: G A Mobley, JM Chambers and Toy Butts constituting 3 majority of said Councilmen.

S A Goodman, Mayor, presided, and L L Parker acted as Clerk. The following resolutions were unanimously adopted:

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF CHIPLEY, GEORGIA, and it is hereby ordained by authority of the same, that an election shall be held in said Town of Chipley, whose corporate name is "The Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley", at all the voting or election precincts within the said Town of Chipley, on the 2Sth day of November, 1919, by the same persons, and in the same manner, and under the same rules and regulations that elections for officers of said Town of Chipley are held.

The purpose of said election is to determine whether or not the qualified voters of said Town of Chipley, by requisite legal majority, shall consent to and authorize the issuance by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley of the following Bonds:

- 1. SEWERAGE BOND in the amount of four thousand ($4,000.00) doilars. For the purpose of providing funds in that amount, which shouldbe applied solely to building and installing a system of sewerage for the said Town of Chipley. Said bonds to be in denominations of one thousand ($1,000.0010 dollars and to bear date December 1st, 1919, and to bear interest at the rate of five and a half (5 1/2) per cent per annum, payable semi-annually on the Ist day of December of each year, said bonds to mature and be paid as follows: One thousand ($1,000.00) dollars on the ist day of each December from 192 to 1927, both inclusive.

- 2. LIGHTING BONDS in the aggregate amount of six thousand ($6,000.00) dollars. For the purpose of providing funds in that amount which will be applied solely to constructing, equipping and installing a system of electric lights and lighting plants for the Town of Chipley, said bonds to be in the denomination of one thousand ($1,000.00) dollars, to bear date of December Ist, 1919, and to bear interest at the rate of five and a half (5 1/2) per cent per annun, payable annually on the Ist day of December of each year. Seid bonds to become due and be paid as follows: One thousand ($1,000.00) dollars on the Ist day of December of each year from 1928 to 1933, both inclusive.

- 3. WATER WORKS BONDS: In the aggregate amount of twenty five thousand ($25,000.00) dollars, for the purpose of providing funds in that amount, which will be applied solely to constructing, equipping and installing a System of water works in the Town of Chipley.

Said bonds to be in denomination of one thousand ($1,000.00)dollars, to bear date December Ist, 1913, to bear interest at the rate of five and a half (5 1/2} per cent per annum, payable annually on the Ist day of December of each year. Said bonds will become due and be paid as follows:

One Thousand ($1,000.00) doliars on the Ist day of December of each year From 1934 to 1940, both inclusive. Two thousand ($2,000.00) doliars on the ist day of December of each year from 1941 to 1943, both inclusive. Both principal and interest of said bonds should be payable in goid coin of the United States, af the present standard of weiqht and fineness, in such place in New York 3s may be specified by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley, pricr to the issuance of said bonds.

Each class of bonds shali be voted on separately.

Those desiring to vote in favor of the issuance of Sewerage Bonds, for the purpose of building and installing a system of Sewerage, Shall do do by casting baliots, having written or printed upon them the words "For Bonds for Sewerage”. Those desiring to vote against the issuance of such Sewerage Bonds shali do so by casting ballots having written or printed upon them “Against Bonds for Sewerage",

Those desiring to vote in favor of the issuance of Lighting Bonds, for the purpose of constructing, equipping and installing a systen of electric lights and lighting plants shali do so by casting ballots having written or printed upon them the words "For Bonds for Lights". Those desiring to vote against the issuance of Lighting Bonds shail do so by casting ballots having written or printed upon them the words “Against Bonds for Lights".

Those desiring to vote in favor of the issuance of Water Works Bonds, for the purpose of equipping and installing a system of Water Works shail do so by casting baiilocts having written or printed upon them the words “For Bonds for Water Works". Those desiring to vote against the issuance of such Water Works Bonds, shali do so by casting ballots having written or printed upon them the words "Against Bonds for Water Works".

The Managers of said election shall make return thereof the the Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley.

BE IT FURTHER ORDAINED that notice of such election shall be given in the Hamiiton Journal, 3 newspaper wherein advertisements of the

Sheriff of Harris County are published thirty (30) days before Said election, by publishing in said newspaper 2 copy of this resolution and ordinance.

BE IT FURTHER ORDAINED that in the event the requisite legal majority of votes are cast in Favor of said bonds, or in favor of either of said bonds, the Mayor and Councii of the Town of Chipley shall issue bonds for each amount and for such purposes as shall be authorized at said election, and the proper officers of the said Town of Chipley are directed to take all proper and requisite steps to secure the validation of said bonds.

Dated this the 23rd day of October, 1919 by order of the Mayor and Council of the Town of Chipley. S A Goodman, Mayor

L L Parker, Clerk
